newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe, AOL shares tumble on deal talk.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe, AOL shares tumble on deal talk.

text.p: Shares of CompuServe Corp and America Online Inc fell on Monday after some negative comments on Wall Street about their ongoing merger talks.

Industry sources confirmed last week that AOL and CompuServe are in merger talks, with AOL looking to buy CompuServe with stock. Monday's Wall Street Journal reported that talks have been in a range of $11 to $14 a share.

"We continue to think a transaction is unlikely at these levels," said Scott Reamer, a Cowen & Co analyst. "We don't know what price is attractive to AOL, but it is not at these levels." CompuServe shares closed off 1-5/8 to 12.
AOL shares tumbled 4-1/8 to 44-1/4, as some analysts said investors were grasping the dilutive impact of an all stock transaction on its earnings going forward.

Earlier AOL issued a statement declining to comment on market rumors and an AOL executive, Myer Berlow, declined to comment on rumors at an Internet Conference held by PaineWebber. But in his remarks, Berlow, who is vice president of interactive marketing, talked about industry consolidation, saying there are too many Internet search engines right now.
A CompuServe spokesman said there was nothing new to add, only that the company's discussions continue.
"We will not say who we are talking with, only that we are still talking," said a CompuServe spokesman in Columbus, Ohio.

One industry source said that AOL has put an offer on the table, but the specific terms could not be learned. CompuServe is believed to be weighing this offer, which is estimated by some analysts to be lower than CompuServe's current stock price of $12. Analysts said they believed CompuServe talked to other potential suitors besides AOL, but it was not clear how serious those discussions had become.
"I'm not too thrilled about it at this point," said Abhishek Gami, a Nesbitt Burns Securities analyst.
